messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] plot.scanone error?
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] plot.scanone error?
messages.body_plain:
If you plot scanone output for a single chromosome, the LOD curve is drawn relative to the marker locations provided in the map, which presumably is not 0.

  pull.map(mapthis3, chr="X")

You can shift the map so that each chromosome starts at 0:

  mapthis3 <- shiftmap(mapthis3)

karl

messages.subject: create linkage groups
messages.subject_clean: create linkage groups
messages.body_plain:
Hi Karl,

I am working with an F2 population to make a genetic map following your manual. It is a population of 53 individuals with ~ 6642 SNPs.  The percent genotyped is 92.8, and the genotypes % for AA is 24.3, for AB is 48.9 and for BB is 26.7. I tried to create the linkage groups but when I ran: draft_gmapf_lg = formLinkageGroups(draft_gmapf, max.rf = 0.35, min.lod = 2.5), the output is:

1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8
6635    1    1    1    1    1    1    1

I tried large values of min.lod , but i still have the same problem, most of the markers fall into the first linkage group.
I checked the expected segregation to remove markers with a below cut-off (geno.table = geno.table(draft_map_SF3),
segreg_dev = geno.table[geno.table$P.value < 0.05/totmar(draft_map_SF3), ], todrop = rownames(geno.table[geno.table$P.value < 1e-5, ]), draft_gmapf = drop.markers(draft_map_SF3, todrop)).

Could you give me any recomendation?

Thank you

Best

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] create linkage groups
messages.subject_clean: [Rqtl-disc] create linkage groups
messages.body_plain:
You’ll seldom get exactly the number of linkage groups as chromosomes.
If min.lod is small, multiple chromosomes will get merged.
If min.lod is large, linkage groups will get broken up.
The appropriate value will depend on sample size and number of markers. But I generally would make it large and have too many linkage groups and then merge them back together later in the map construction process.

karl

That's not the case for the rest of QTLs. I am guessing effectplot() gives me contrast between genotypes based on that single marker but fitqtl() takes the whole model into consideration (I have 8 QTLs in total). Thus I would believe that QTL has a genative effect. Could you please provide some insights? Thank you in advance!

Best,
Jiayang

For a 4-way cross, the mother and father are assumed to have genotypes AB and CD, respectively. karl
